hints.query: Test rule runs this query against real data from the last six hours.
hints.thresholds: The highest matching severity wins; duration is converted to evaluation periods.

hints.delay: How far back each round looks, waiting for data that arrives late or is not written out yet. Auto: none on a single process, the platform setting in a cluster.

hints.urgency: Left unset, the escalation policy the incident goes to decides.
hints.home_cluster: In a federation, every cluster counts the records written to it. Choose one cluster to add up the counts of all clusters mapped to this organization and open the incidents there; the others only count.

anomaly.subtitle: Detect outliers against a same-time-of-day baseline (MAD).
anomaly.detection_description: Each interval the query's first numeric value is compared against the baseline.
anomaly.detector_description: Median Absolute Deviation builds a robust baseline from recent same-time history.

hints.name: Shown on incidents this rule opens.
hints.service: Optional label used for cross-signal context.
hints.query: Return a single numeric value (e.g. avg / p95 / count).
hints.algorithm: MAD (robust median) or EWMA (tracks recent drift).
hints.lookback_days: Days of same-time-of-day history for the baseline (1-30).
hints.k: Higher = less sensitive. Fires when |value - baseline| > k·σ.
hints.alpha: EWMA only: higher = weights recent samples more (0-1).
hints.for_periods: Consecutive anomalous intervals before an incident opens.
hints.weekly_seasonality: Compare only the same weekday's history — cuts weekday/weekend false positives. Needs lookback >= 7 (28+ recommended).
hints.source: Watch the result of a query, or an APM figure of a service

email.description: How a mail becomes an alert. Status words, severities, times and percentages in the subject stay out of the dedup key, so the problem and recovery mails of one alert land on one incident.
email.senders_hint: Comma separated: addresses, or @example.com for a whole domain; * accepts everyone. Required with a mailbox, or anyone who knows the address could open incidents.
email.resolve_hint: A regular expression. Empty takes the built-in one: resolved, recovered, recovery, cleared, 恢复, 已解决, and OK at the start.
email.dedup_hint: A regular expression; its first group is taken. Empty or no match uses the tidied subject.
email.ignore_hint: A regular expression. Mail that matches is skipped; empty skips nothing.

mailbox.title: Read a mailbox
mailbox.description: Read only: nothing is marked as read or deleted. It starts from the moment it first connects; mail already there does not count.
mailbox.elsewhere: The mailbox is read by this source's receiving cluster, {{cluster}}. Set it up there: the password stays in that cluster.
mailbox.plaintext_warning: Without encryption the password crosses the network in the clear. Use it only on a network you trust.
mailbox.auth_password_hint: The mailbox password, or an app password from the provider.
mailbox.auth_oauth2_hint: A token from client credentials: Microsoft 365 no longer takes passwords.
mailbox.poll_hint: 15 to 3600. Some mail servers limit frequent sign-ins.
mailbox.saved: Mailbox saved; it is read from the next round
mailbox.not_read_yet: Not read yet; it starts in the next round.

setup_guide.api: Send alerts with the request below. A trigger, acknowledgement and recovery with the same dedup_key land on one incident.
setup_guide.alertmanager: Add the receiver below to alertmanager.yml and route alerts to it. Keep send_resolved true.
setup_guide.grafana: Add a webhook contact point under Alerting → Contact points as below, then use it in a notification policy.
setup_guide.datadog: Create a webhook under Integrations → Webhooks as below, then mention @webhook-<name> in a monitor's message.
setup_guide.pagerduty: Create a webhook under Integrations → Generic Webhooks (v3) as below.
setup_guide.aliyun_cms: Enter the intake address as the alarm callback of an alarm rule, or as the webhook address of an event subscription push channel for system events.
setup_guide.tencent_monitor: Enter the intake address as the API callback of a notification template under Alarm Management, then bind the template to an alarm policy.
setup_guide.aws_cloudwatch: Have the alarm's state changes go to an SNS topic, and add an HTTPS subscription to the topic with the intake address (the AWS CLI form is below). The subscription confirms itself; leave Raw message delivery off. Send the OK state to the topic too, or incidents will not resolve on their own.
setup_guide.zabbix: Save this as YAML and import it under Alerts → Media types. Give a user this media (Send to can be anything), then add a trigger action whose operations, recovery operations and update operations go to that user.
setup_guide.email: For when a mailbox cannot be read: a mail system you already run (Postfix, SES, Mailgun) posts the raw message like this, and it is read the same way.

incident_actions.no_policy: This incident has no escalation policy.
incident_actions.snooze_description: No notifications while snoozed; when it ends, the incident goes back to unacknowledged and its assignees are notified again. An unacknowledged incident is acknowledged first.
incident_actions.merge_description: Merged incidents no longer notify or escalate on their own and are resolved with the main one; a merge cannot be undone.

incident_timeline.remediation_unverified: Remediation action “{{action}}” did not pass its check

kinds.kubernetes_hint: Restarts or scales a workload on a registered cluster, or rolls a Deployment back one revision.

clusters.name: Name

run.title: Run “{{name}}”

run.needs_two: Two people who can approve have to approve it; it runs right after.

tickets.webhook_address: Jira webhook address (add it under Webhooks in Jira's system settings, with the connector's webhook secret)

drawer.subtitle: Credentials are kept encrypted and not shown again; leave one empty to keep it.

drawer.resolve_transition_hint: A transition's name or ID; empty takes the first one to a done status.
drawer.webhook_secret_hint: Jira's webhook is taken only with a secret (X-Hub-Signature is checked); without one, statuses are synced every 5 minutes.

comments.resolved: Comment when the incident is resolved
comments.notes: Write the incident's notes as comments

drawer.transition_on_resolve: Move the ticket to done when the incident is resolved
drawer.resolve_when_done: Resolve the incident when the ticket is done
drawer.on_major: Make a ticket when a major incident is declared

drawer.table_hint: incident by default; it must extend task.
drawer.auth_oauth_hint: The instance must allow the client credentials grant.

major.hint: Declare it when the impact is wide and several people work on it: roles, a war room and meeting, a checklist and one stream of updates.
major.declared_by_rule: Declared major by the organization's rule
major.update_hint: Goes to the war room and to the stakeholders, roles and assignees.

settings.title: Major incident settings
settings.subtitle: How a declared major incident gets its war room, meeting and tasks, who hears its updates, and which incidents are major from the start.
settings.war_room_hint: A notify connector that can make group chats (Feishu App, Slack App, DingTalk, WeCom) makes the chat and adds the assignees, roles and stakeholders, by the identities each linked to it.
settings.checklist_hint: Tasks added when it is declared, one per line.
settings.stakeholders_hint: People not working on it who need to know how it goes, such as managers, customer success or PR. Updates notify them (besides the assignees and roles), and war rooms add them.
settings.auto_hint: A new incident that matches is major from the start.

room_notes.dingtalk_app: In DingTalk, the app's robot has to be added to the group before updates can be posted to it; group names are at most 20 characters.
room_notes.wecom_app: The WeCom app has to be visible to the root department; a group has at least two people and no join link, and members find it in WeCom.

meeting_hints.feishu_vc: The Feishu App books a 6-hour Feishu meeting owned by the commander. The app needs permission to reserve video meetings.
meeting_hints.tencent_meeting: Create a self-built app in the Tencent Meeting enterprise console for its AppId, SdkId, SecretId and SecretKey; a 6-hour meeting is booked under the member below.
meeting_hints.zoom: Create a Server-to-Server OAuth app in the Zoom App Marketplace with permission to create meetings (meeting:write:meeting:admin); an instant meeting is started with the user below as host.
meeting_hints.google_meet: A service account creates meetings for the organizer: in the Google Workspace admin console, give it domain-wide delegation for https://www.googleapis.com/auth/meetings.space.created.

settings.secret_kept: Set; leave empty to keep it

google.organizer_hint: Meetings are created on this person's behalf

rule_transfer.import_subtitle: Paste or choose a rule bundle exported from MoleSignal, or a Prometheus alerting rule file (PrometheusRule too). Try it first to see what each rule would do, then write it all at once.
rule_transfer.content_hint: JSON or YAML. Rules are matched by name: a new name is created, a known one updated.
rule_transfer.create_only: Only create; leave those with a name that exists as they are
rule_transfer.has_errors: fix the rules with errors, then import

transfer.unknown_members: These emails have no member in this workspace:

findings.schedules_only: Only schedules come over. Escalation policies, routing rules and overrides are left out.
findings.shift_based_not_listed: The file does not list PagerDuty's shift-based schedules, which the V2 API does not return, so they may be missing here. The migration script lists them.
findings.shift_based_not_fetched: The file only names this shift-based schedule and has none of its content, so it is left out. Run the migration script again, or fetch it with GET /v3/schedules/{id}.
findings.timezone_unknown: The timezone "{{timezone}}" is not an IANA name.
findings.layers_missing: The file has no layers for this schedule. Fetch it with GET /schedules/{id}.
findings.rotations_missing: The file has no rotations for this schedule. Fetch it with GET /v2/schedules/{id}.
findings.events_missing: The file has no rotations and events for this schedule. Fetch it with GET /v3/schedules/{id}.
findings.user_without_email: {{rotation}}: the file has no email for {{user}}.
findings.participant_team: {{rotation}}: team {{name}} takes a turn, and a rotation here only takes people.
findings.participant_escalation: {{rotation}}: escalation {{name}} takes a turn, and a rotation here only takes people.
findings.participant_none: {{rotation}}: a turn belongs to no one, which a rotation here cannot leave open.
findings.rotations_overlap: {{rotation}} and {{other}} overlap, first at {{at}}. Both people would be on call in the source, and a schedule here has one at a time; move them to separate schedules.
findings.every_member_on_call: {{rotation}}: all its members are on call at once, and a schedule here has one at a time; move them to separate schedules.
findings.recurrence_unsupported: {{rotation}}: the recurrence {{value}} cannot be written as a rotation.
findings.shifts_per_member_unsupported: {{rotation}}: each member takes {{value}} shifts in a row and a week has {{per_week}}, so handoffs do not fall on a fixed period, which a rotation here needs.
findings.event_timezones_differ: {{rotation}} uses {{timezone}} and {{other}} uses {{other_timezone}}. A schedule here has one timezone; move them to separate schedules.
findings.timezone_from_events: The schedule's timezone is {{schedule_timezone}} and its events use {{timezone}}. It uses {{timezone}} here, so handoffs stay at the same time.
findings.custom_shifts_one: {{count}} custom shift from now on: {{at}} to {{until}}, {{user}}. A rotation here cannot express a one-off shift. Import after it has passed, or remove it from final_schedule in the file and add an override after importing.
findings.custom_shifts_other: {{count}} custom shifts from now on, the first {{at}} to {{until}}, {{user}}. A rotation here cannot express one-off shifts. Import after they have passed, or remove them from final_schedule in the file and add overrides after importing.
findings.rendered_several_on_call: From {{at}} to {{until}} the source has {{first}} and {{second}} on call at once, and a schedule here has one at a time.
findings.rotation_type_unsupported: {{rotation}}: the rotation type {{value}} is not known.
findings.rotation_length_invalid: {{rotation}}: the rotation length {{value}} cannot be used.
findings.restriction_unsupported: {{rotation}}: the time restriction {{value}} cannot be written as weekly ranges.
findings.rendered_in_other_zone: {{rotation}}: the response was rendered in another timezone ({{value}}), so its restrictions cannot be read in the schedule's. Fetch it with GET /schedules/{id} and no time_zone.
findings.starts_before_handoff: {{rotation}}: the layer starts before its rotation does, and who is on call until then is not known.
findings.rendered_mismatch: Differs from the source from {{at}} to {{until}}: the source has {{expected}}, this import would have {{actual}}.
findings.rotation_ended: {{rotation}} ended at {{at}}: left out, it no longer decides who is on call.
findings.too_many_rotations: One schedule has more than {{limit}} rotations.
findings.schedule_paused: Disabled in the source: it comes over paused and was not compared.
findings.rotation_empty: {{rotation}} has nobody on it or never applies: left out.
findings.team_not_carried: Team {{name}} is not carried over: none has that name here, or the schedule already has one. Who is on call does not change.
findings.rendered_matched: Compared with the source from {{from}} to {{to}}: the same people on call.
findings.rendered_missing: Not compared: the file has no schedule rendered by the source. Check who is on call after importing.
findings.rendered_stale: Not compared: the schedule rendered by the source is all in the past. Fetch it again.
findings.clock_change_not_compared: The comparison does not reach a clock change in {{timezone}}: handoffs after the next one were not compared.
findings.overrides_left_out_one: {{count}} override in the compared stretch is not imported.
findings.overrides_left_out_other: {{count}} overrides in the compared stretch are not imported.

policies.import_subtitle: A `molesignal.escalation-policies/v1` bundle. Matched by name: a new name is created, a known one updated; try it first, then import.
policies.content_hint: JSON or YAML. Users are named by email; schedules, teams and holiday calendars by name.

schedules.import_subtitle: A `molesignal.schedules/v1` bundle, or the schedules of Opsgenie or PagerDuty as their APIs return them. Matched by name: a new name is created, a known one updated; try it first, then import.
schedules.content_hint: JSON or YAML. Members are named by email, teams and holiday calendars by name. Overrides and swaps are not in the file; an update keeps them.
schedules.has_errors: fix the schedules with errors, then import
schedules.migration_intro: Run this script wherever curl and jq are available, then choose the file it writes. The API key stays there: MoleSignal does not keep it and never calls the other tool.
schedules.migration_key: Set {{name}} first; a key that can read is enough.
schedules.migration_docs: What comes over and what does not

routing.import_subtitle: A `molesignal.routing-rules/v1` bundle. Matched by name: a new name is created, a known one updated; try it first, then import.
routing.content_hint: JSON or YAML. Escalation policies, teams and holiday calendars are named by name. The rules of the file go first, in its order; the others keep theirs after them.
